rite.prompt: How many paths of wisdom does the Tree of the Sephiroth comprehend, in Hall?

signal:
SEPHIRTH.NFO                                       HALL 1.3
================================================================
The Tree of the Sephiroth
Manly P. Hall · 1928 · folio p.372 · ECHO QBL.TREE

THESIS
  Ten globes, three pillars, twenty-two paths. A filing system
  for God, the world, and the person, drawn as a tree.

POINTS
  * 10 sephiroth + 22 letters = 32 paths of wisdom
  * Greater Face / Lesser Face; the abyss of Daath
  * Pillars of Mercy, Severity, Mildness
  * The four-letter Name as the tree's spine
  * Kircher's engraving is the map most Western occultists stole

SEE ALSO  qabbalah  tarot  cosmogony  human-body
DEGREE    NEOPHYTE may read this screen
================================================================
translation:
If the previous chapter is the claim, this one is the furniture. Ten sephiroth (emanations, “numbers,” globes) hang on three pillars: Mercy on the right, Severity on the left, Mildness down the middle. Twenty-two paths join them — one path per Hebrew letter, later one tarot trump per path. Together they are the thirty-two paths of wisdom from Yetzirah.

Hall flags Daath, the non-sephirah in the abyss, as the knowledge that is not a globe you can sit in. He distinguishes the Greater Face (the tree as it is in the Infinite) from the Lesser Face (the tree as it shows up in a person). The four letters of the Name — Yod He Vav He — are treated as a vertical formula: the same tree spoken as a word.

Athanasius Kircher’s seventeenth-century engraving is the picture Western esotericism never recovered from. Hall reproduces the type. Codex, on this lot, already draws a four-color SVG of it. HALL does not redraw that gadget. HALL treats the tree as a filesystem: files live in globes, SEE ALSO links are paths. `read sephiroth` is the legend for a map we will hang in DH0: later.
